strings.help.text:
1. On the left, choose a key or a knob action.
2. On the right, choose what it should do.
3. Click “Write to device”.
4. Check the result in “Device → Input monitor” (F8).

Actions marked ✓ are stored in the keyboard itself and work even without the program.

Actions marked ⚙ the keyboard cannot do on its own (on the new CH552 revision: multimedia, mouse, key sequences and all system actions). For them the device sends a service key F13–F24, and {0} running in the tray performs the action. Turn on “Settings → Start with Windows” so this always works.

Layouts are kept in presets — switch them in the window header. Writing works only over a USB cable. No Windows driver is needed — the standard one is used.

strings.wizard.intro:
The wizard writes test letters to the keyboard and asks you to press each key and the knob in turn. From the letters it learns whether writing works and which numbers the knob has on your board.

First, unplug the USB cable and plug it back in — the wizard will notice it by itself. About a minute.
